passages.title: A Chess Game with Grandma
paragraphs: Grandma asked me to play chess after dinner. I knew how the pieces moved, but I always tried to capture something straight away. Grandma moved more slowly. Before touching a piece, she studied the whole board. Soon, my king was in danger（危险）. “Look at what might happen next,” she said. We started another game, and this time I took my time. I still lost, but I kept my queen much longer. Now I enjoy the quiet thinking between moves. A good decision（决定） sometimes begins with a short pause（停顿）.

passages.title: Our Classroom Time Capsule
paragraphs: We filled a metal box with things from our school year. I added a bus ticket, while Emma chose a class timetable. Our teacher called it a time capsule（胶囊）. We also included a list of our favourite games and the price of a school lunch. We sealed（密封） the box and left it in a school cupboard. A label said, “Open in ten years.” I wonder which things will seem strange then. Perhaps our favourite game will be out of date. I hope the box will bring back happy memories.

passages.title: The Swimming Bag Checklist
paragraphs: I reached the swimming pool with my towel and swimsuit, but my goggles were still at home. Without them, my lesson was less comfortable. That evening, I made a checklist（检查清单） and tied it to my swimming bag. Before each lesson, I go through the list and check every item. I also use it afterwards, so nothing stays behind in the changing room. Last week, the list helped me remember my wet towel. A routine（固定做法） may seem boring（无聊的）, but it saves me from making the same mistake over and over again.

passages.title: A Poster with Fewer Words
paragraphs: I made a poster for our school art show. I filled it with bright pictures and long sentences. From close up, it looked wonderful. From across the classroom, nobody could read the date. My partner suggested making the most important information larger. We crossed out some words and left more empty space. We also moved the date below the title. The new poster looked simpler, but its message（信息） was clearer. When we put it by the stairs, pupils stopped to read it. Good design（设计） helps people notice what matters（重要）.

passages.title: The Lunch Table Vote
paragraphs: Our class wanted to choose a name for its new lunch table group. We suggested names of animals, colours and stars. Everyone liked a different idea, and the discussion grew noisy. Our teacher gave us each a small piece of paper. We wrote down one choice and put it in a box. Then two pupils counted the votes（选票）. “The Blue Whales” won by one vote. It was not my favourite name, but I agreed to use it. Making a group choice（选择） also means accepting（接受） a result we do not prefer.

passages.title: My First Pottery Bowl
paragraphs: At a pottery（陶艺） class, I tried to make a round bowl from wet clay. Mine leaned to one side, and the edge was uneven. I wanted to start again. The teacher turned it slowly and asked, “What could this shape become?” I added a tail and two ears. Now it looked like a sleeping cat. We left our work to dry before the teacher fired it in a special oven. Weeks later, I brought my bowl home. It was far from perfect, but its uneven（不平整的） shape gave it character（特色）.

passages.title: The Class Weather Reporter
paragraphs: For a week, I was our class weather reporter. Each morning, I checked the temperature and described the sky. On Wednesday, I wrote “sunny” before breakfast. By lunchtime, dark clouds covered the school. Our teacher reminded me that a weather report describes conditions at a particular（特定的） time. A forecast（预报） tells us what may happen later. They are not quite the same. I added the time to my notes and checked again after lunch. Now I pay attention to changes throughout（贯穿） the day, rather than choosing one word for the whole morning.

passages.title: A Quiet Corner for Everyone
paragraphs: Our classroom was often noisy before lessons. Some pupils enjoyed talking, while others wanted a quiet place to finish reading. We came up with a plan: one corner would be quiet, and the other side could be used for conversation. We moved two desks and made a small sign. Nobody had to stay in one place all morning. The new arrangement gave us a choice（选择）. I sometimes chatted first and then moved to the quiet corner. Sharing a room became easier when we made space for different needs（需要） and preferences（偏好）.

passages.title: The Word I Could Not Pronounce
paragraphs: I met the word “island” in a story and read every letter aloud. My brother smiled and said the letter s was silent. I checked a dictionary and listened to the word carefully. Then I broke it down into smaller sounds and practised saying it in a sentence. The next day, I recognised it immediately. English spelling can sometimes be puzzling（令人困惑的）. Now, when I find an unfamiliar word, I do not just guess. I check its pronunciation（发音） and meaning together. Hearing a word helps me remember how it looks too.

passages.title: The Day We Changed Partners
paragraphs: In art class, our teacher asked us to work with someone new. I usually chose my best friend, so I felt unsure. My new partner was quiet, and I did not know what to say. We began making a paper city. I liked designing buildings, while she was good at making tiny vehicles. Soon, roads connected our houses, and a little bus stood beside the station. We did not talk all the time, but we worked well together. By the end, I discovered（发现） a different kind of friendship（友谊） through a shared task（任务）.

passages.title: What Is Inside a Seed?
paragraphs: A dry bean may look lifeless, but there is a tiny young plant inside. The bean also contains a supply of food to help it begin growing. Its outer coat offers protection（保护）. When conditions are right, the seed takes in water and starts to grow. A small root comes out first, followed by a shoot（嫩芽）. Our teacher showed us pictures of these stages. I drew each one in my notebook. Next time I hold a bean, I will think of the small beginning inside it, waiting for its chance（机会）.

passages.title: Why We See Lightning First
paragraphs: During a storm, I saw a bright flash before I heard thunder. Dad explained that both come from the same event, but light travels much faster than sound. That is why the flash reaches us first. When a storm is farther away, the gap（间隔） between the flash and the sound is usually longer. We watched from safely inside the house, away from the window. I listened for the next rumble. The sky was giving us a lesson about speed（速度）, and we did not even need to step outside for the demonstration（演示）.

passages.title: A Paper Fan on a Hot Day
paragraphs: On a warm afternoon, I folded a piece of paper into a fan. Waving it made my face feel cooler. The fan did not produce cold air. It moved air across my skin, helping sweat（汗水） evaporate（蒸发） and carry heat away. A breeze（微风） can help in a similar way. My little sister tried using a tiny card as a fan, but it moved less air. We compared our fans and laughed at how hard she waved hers. A simple piece of paper can make a difference when we understand how to use it.

passages.title: The Changing Shape of Ice
paragraphs: Our teacher put an ice cube in a shallow dish. We measured its width and drew its shape. After a while, the corners became rounder, and water appeared around it. The ice was melting（融化）. It was still water, but its form was changing from solid to liquid. Later, we poured the water into a star-shaped tray and put it in the freezer. The next day, we had a little ice star. Water does not keep its shape like ice does. It takes the shape of its container（容器） when it is liquid（液态的）.

passages.title: A Snail after the Rain
paragraphs: After the rain, a snail moved slowly across our garden path. I bent down to watch without touching it. Its soft body slid over a shiny trail. The snail makes mucus（黏液）, which helps it move and protects its body from rough surfaces. Its shell provides a place to hide away when danger comes. I waited until it reached the grass before walking on. The journey was short for me but long for such a small creature. Watching it made me notice the surface（表面） of the path in a new way.

passages.title: How a Map Uses Symbols
paragraphs: A real town has thousands of details, but a map cannot show them all. Instead, it uses symbols（符号） to stand for important places. A small tent may show a campsite, while a blue line may show a river. We need to check the key because symbols can differ between maps. In class, we designed a map of an imaginary island. I used a star for a treasure cave and explained it in the key（图例）. My friend found the cave easily. Clear symbols help a reader make sense of a complicated（复杂的） place.

passages.title: The Clothes Repair Shop
paragraphs: There is a small repair shop near our block. Yesterday, I took a jacket there because its zip would not close. The owner looked closely and found a bent part. While she worked, I noticed boxes of buttons in many colours. She explained that a missing button or a broken zip does not always mean we need new clothes. Soon, my jacket closed properly again. I thanked her and put it on. A careful repair（修补） saved a favourite jacket, and I learned to value（珍惜） the skill（技艺） behind such small jobs.

passages.title: A Museum without Glass Cases
paragraphs: At an outdoor museum, we walked through old houses and a small workshop. Some rooms were furnished as they were many years ago. A guide showed us a heavy iron that people heated before using. There were no buttons or wires. I imagined the work needed to smooth a shirt. We could not touch every object, but the rooms helped us picture everyday life in the past. History was more than a list of dates. It was also about how people made a living, managed their chores（家务） and used the tools（工具） they had.

passages.title: The Bakery at Dawn
paragraphs: On a school visit, we entered a bakery early in the morning. The baker was shaping soft dough（面团） into long rolls. Some trays were waiting, while others were already in the oven. He explained that the dough needs time to rise. We watched through a safe viewing window as pale rolls slowly turned golden. The warm smell filled the room. By opening time, rows of fresh bread were ready for sale. I never realised how much preparation（准备） happened before the first customer arrived. Behind a familiar breakfast was a carefully planned（安排好的） morning of work.

passages.title: A Book in Two Languages
paragraphs: I borrowed a picture book with two languages on each page. One was English, and the other was Chinese. At first, I read only the Chinese lines. Then I covered them and tried the English. The pictures helped when a sentence was difficult. I noticed that the two versions did not always use exactly the same number of words. A translation（译文） needs to carry the meaning, not just translate word for word. After reading, I tried to retell the story in English. The second language gave me support without doing all the thinking（思考） for me.

passages.title: The Bell on the Cat’s Collar
paragraphs: Our cat wore a collar with a little bell. One evening, I heard it ringing under the sofa, but the cat was sitting beside me. I stared at him in surprise. Then my little brother crawled out, holding the collar. “It fell off,” he said. “I was trying to find the bell.” We laughed at my mistake. I was so used to connecting that sound with the cat that I did not check the facts. A familiar signal（信号） can be useful, but it does not always tell the whole story（实情）.

passages.title: The Squirrel and the Borrowed Ladder
paragraphs: A squirrel borrowed a ladder from a hedgehog（刺猬） to reach a high shelf. After finishing, he left it outside his own door. The next morning, the hedgehog came looking for it. “I was going to return it,” said the squirrel. “But I needed it yesterday,” replied the hedgehog. The squirrel carried it back and apologised（道歉）. Later, when he borrowed a basket, he asked when it was needed and returned it before sunset. Borrowing（借用） is more than getting permission（允许）. It also means taking care of things and keeping track of when they should go back.

passages.title: The Surprise inside the Trophy
paragraphs: Our football team received an old trophy（奖杯） from the school cupboard for a display. As we cleaned it, a folded paper fell out of the base. It listed the names of a team from twenty years ago. Our sports teacher pointed to one name and smiled. It was his! He told us about their muddy final match and the friends he still knew. We placed the paper beside the trophy. Suddenly, the shiny cup meant more to us. It held a memory（回忆） of people who once stood in our shoes, full of hope（希望）.

passages.title: A Dragon That Was Afraid of Heights
paragraphs: A young dragon loved looking at clouds, but he was afraid to fly high. The other dragons invited him to race, and he always stayed behind. One day, an older dragon asked him to try a short flight above the grass. They landed after a few seconds and tried again. There was no race and no laughing. Slowly, the young dragon began enjoying the view. He did not reach the clouds that day. Still, he discovered that being brave（勇敢的） could mean taking one small step at a time, with a little encouragement（鼓励）.

passages.title: The Wrong Size of Box
paragraphs: We needed a box for our class model ship. I chose the biggest one I could find, but it was too wide to carry through the classroom door easily. A smaller box seemed perfect until we tried its lid. The ship’s tall mast（桅杆） would not fit. Finally, we measured the model before searching again. The third box worked. We packed soft paper around the ship and carried it together. Guessing felt quicker at first, but measuring（测量） saved us trouble. The right size depends on more than just one dimension（尺寸）.

passages.title: The Joke That Went Too Far
paragraphs: I made a joke about my friend’s new haircut, and several classmates laughed. I laughed too, until I noticed that he was quiet. At break time, I asked if something was wrong. “I liked my hair before everyone laughed,” he said. I felt ashamed（惭愧的）. I apologised and told the others my joke was unkind. My friend did not smile immediately, and I did not expect him to. I needed to show more respect（尊重）. Now I think twice before making someone else the centre of a joke, even when I want to be funny.

passages.title: The Shop with an Honesty Box
paragraphs: During a countryside walk, we found a table of apples beside a farm gate. A sign showed the price, but nobody was standing there. A small locked box had a slot（狭缝） for money. Mum explained that it was an honesty（诚实） box. We chose a bag, counted our coins and put the correct amount inside. The farmer was working nearby and waved when we left. The little shop depended on customers doing the right thing without being watched. I liked the apples, but I also remembered the quiet trust（信任） behind that simple way of life.

passages.title: Two Solutions to One Problem
paragraphs: Our teacher asked us to build a paper bridge between two books. My flat sheet fell down when I placed a rubber on it. I folded another sheet into a zigzag（锯齿形）, and it held the rubber. Across the room, another group rolled paper into tubes（管状物） and made a bridge that worked too. We compared the shapes and tested them with more rubbers. There was no single design everyone had to copy. Different solutions（解决办法） could solve the same problem. I learned to keep an open mind and explain my ideas through evidence（证据）.

passages.title: The Photograph I Did Not Take
paragraphs: At the zoo, I wanted a photograph of a red panda. It stayed behind a tree, so I waited with my camera ready. Then it climbed onto a branch and began washing its face. For a moment, I forgot the camera and simply watched. By the time I lifted it, the animal was hidden again. I felt disappointed, but Dad asked what I remembered. I described its paws, soft tail and careful movements. I had no picture to show, yet I still had a clear memory（回忆）. Sometimes paying attention is its own reward（回报）.

passages.title: Our Last Page of the Term
paragraphs: On the last day of term, our teacher asked us to leave one page in our notebooks for questions. We could write anything we still wondered about. Mine included, “How do birds know where to go?” and “Why do some songs stay in my head?” Nobody had to answer everything that afternoon. We read a few questions aloud and discovered new things to explore. Finishing a notebook did not mean finishing our learning（学习）. I went home with an empty schoolbag and a head full of possibilities（可能性）, ready to find out a little more.
